newsitem.title: USA: Hutchison Whampoa $2.0 bln debt deal sets records.
newsitem.headline: Hutchison Whampoa $2.0 bln debt deal sets records.

text.p: Blue chip Hong Kong firm Hutchison Whampoa Ltd sold $2.0 billion in debt on Thursday, setting a new record as the largest-ever global issue of Yankee bonds by a non-U.S. company, according to Carlos Cordeiro, managing director at Goldman, Sachs & Co, one of the lead underwriters of the deal.
"The enthusiasm this issue met in the market really speaks to the credit and the future of Hong Kong in so much as we are just barely 30 days into the new adminstration," Cordeiro said.
The multi-tranche 144A/Eurobond offering was Hutchison's debut in the corporate bond market and met with very strong demand from insitutional investors from around the world.

Even after increasing the deal to $2.0 billion from an original size of $1.0 billion, the company was not even close to filling all the orders from investors. Cordeiro said the total size of the book for the offering was $7 billion.
Once the deal was completed, Goldman Sachs and co-lead underwriter Merrill Lynch & Co placed roughly 50 percent of the bonds in the U.S., 25 percent in Europe and 25 percent in Asia.
"We are delighted with the Asian response, particulary given the fact that this is an Asian credit," Cordeiro said.
Cordeiro said the deal was indicative of a dramatic surge in demand for fixed-income securities from Asian investors over the last six months.
He noted the bonds were sold to a broad range of Asian investors residing in places such as Hong Kong and China, Singapore, Taiwan and South Korea.
Cordeiro said a $750 million 10-year tranche, the largest of the offering, met with widespread investor interest, while longer-maturity tranches saw stronger U.S. investor interest.
He noted the deal also set a record as the longest maturity ever offered by a Hong Kong corporate issuer.
The other tranches consisted of $500 million in 20-year bonds, $500 million in 30-year bonds and $250 million in 40-year bonds, puttable in 12 years.
Analysts have said the issue, becuase of its large size and structure, is likely to be used as as a benchmark for future Asian offerings.
Hutchison and its dealers mounted a massive roadshow to market the deal. The tour began just over a week ago in Hong Kong and included many cities in the U.S. and Europe.
"Once people picked up on the story, we had an easy job selling the deal," said Cordeiro.
"The company enjoys the highest ratings of anyone in Hong Kong equivalent to the sovereign ceiling. It is really one of Hong Kong's premier corporate credits," he added.
The issue was rated A3 by Moody's Investors Service and A-plus by Standard & Poor's.
The bonds were issued by Hutchison Whampoa Finance Ltd, a unit of Hutchison Whampoa. The bonds are guaranteed by the parent company.
Hutchison is a diversified company which owns trade ports and telecommunications businesses around the world.
The company owns a majority stake in Hong Kong International Terminals (HIT), the world's largest privately owned container terminal operator and the largest port operator in Hong Kong.
Moody's said, "HIT is also strategically well-positioned to grow with the development of trade passing through the principal ports in southern China."
Hutchison also operates the largest port in the United Kingdom, the Port of Felixstowe.
-Douglas Brown, U.S. Corporate Bond Unit, 212-895-1662
